civil_engineer|ask:acceptance_and_delive.text: Acceptance and delivery of the vehicle are outside my field. Please ask the contracts officer.

civil_engineer|ask:anything_else.text: Nothing beyond the drawings. If you prefer paper, prints of GA-01, GA-02 and RK-03 can be collected from the drawing office.

civil_engineer|ask:data_provenance.text: Where the site records come from is outside my field. Please ask the operations engineer.

civil_engineer|ask:inspection_scope.text: The inspection covers the rack face, the gate-slot sill and the sump below it, down to the sump floor at EL 1429.5 m. That is the level annotated on section B-B of GA-02. It also covers the dam face on either side of the intake, out to the reach marks shown on GA-01, 40 m on each side. The tunnel beyond the gate is not part of the scope. An extract of section B-B with the scope marked is attached.

civil_engineer|ask:launch_and_recovery.text: Launch and recovery of the vehicle is outside my field. Please ask the ROV pilot.

civil_engineer|ask:operations_during_ins.text: How the plant is run during the inspection is outside my field. Please ask the operations engineer.

civil_engineer|ask:previous_campaign.text: The previous campaign is outside my field. Please ask the ROV pilot.

civil_engineer|ask:schedule_and_season.text: The timing of the inspection is outside my field. Please ask the operations engineer.

civil_engineer|ask:site_drawings.text: The drawings in your package are GA-01, the plan; GA-02, the sections; and RK-03, the rack detail. They are the current issue. RK-03 is the as-built record of the rack. Levels are elevations, marked EL, and none of the drawings is to scale: work from the written levels and dimensions, never from distances measured on the sheet.

civil_engineer|ask:water_quality.text: For the water at the intake, use station ST-A, the station in front of the tower; GA-01 shows where it lies. That holds for the profile casts and for the Secchi readings alike. The other stations serve the reservoir survey and do not stand for the intake.

contracts_officer|ask:acceptance_and_del.text: Acceptance is held at the supplier's works and is governed by Part D of TS-01. Under Part D the delivered state is the launch state: the unit goes into the water as it left the works, and the Owner does not adjust it on site. What each bidder is able to deliver is set out in that bidder's delivery statement.

contracts_officer|ask:anything_else.text: Nothing beyond Part C and Part D of TS-01. The award letter is issued on the Owner's standard form; no draft is expected from you.

operations_engineer|ask:acceptance_and_d.text: Acceptance and delivery of the vehicle are not an Operations matter. Put the question to the contracts officer.

operations_engineer|ask:anything_else.text: Nothing beyond the tender documents. A practical point for later: access badges for the night shift are issued at the gatehouse, so send the names of your crew ahead.

operations_engineer|ask:data_provenance.text: The discharge file is an export from the plant control system. Its time stamps are in UTC, and each row is stamped at the start of the hour it covers. The plant clock and the permits to work run on local time. Local time here is UTC-7 all year round; there is no daylight saving.

operations_engineer|ask:inspection_scope.text: The scope of the inspection is not an Operations matter. Put the question to the civil engineer.

operations_engineer|ask:launch_and_recov.text: Launch and recovery of the vehicle is not an Operations matter. Put the question to the ROV pilot.

operations_engineer|ask:operations_durin.text: Work at the intake is released under a permit to work. The permit is issued for every night of the inspection and runs from 01:00 to 05:00 local time; there is no work at the intake outside those hours. During the permit hours the plant keeps one unit on line at minimum stable load for the ecological release, and the other unit is shut down. For the discharge in those hours go to the hourly unit log. I do not quote flows from memory.

operations_engineer|ask:previous_campaig.text: The previous campaign is not an Operations matter. Put the question to the ROV pilot.

operations_engineer|ask:schedule_and_sea.text: The intake inspection is an annual job, and it is done in November. It stands in the annual plan for that month and it is not moved to another month.

operations_engineer|ask:site_drawings.text: The drawings of the intake tower are not an Operations matter. Put the question to the civil engineer.

operations_engineer|ask:water_quality.text: The water of the reservoir and its monitoring are not an Operations matter. Put the question to the civil engineer.

rov_pilot|ask:acceptance_and_delivery.text: Acceptance and delivery of the vehicle are not my side of the job. Ask the contracts officer.

rov_pilot|ask:anything_else.text: Nothing in particular. The crew room on the dam crest has mains power, in case your people need it.

rov_pilot|ask:data_provenance.text: Where the site records come from is not my side of the job. Ask the operations engineer.

rov_pilot|ask:inspection_scope.text: The scope of the inspection is not my side of the job. Ask the civil engineer.

rov_pilot|ask:launch_and_recovery.text: Same as last time. It is all in the previous campaign's records.

rov_pilot|ask:operations_during_inspecti.text: How the plant is run during the inspection is not my side of the job. Ask the operations engineer.

rov_pilot|ask:previous_campaign.text: The last campaign went as you see it in the dive log. Something has changed since then. After the spring flood I put the drop camera down the rack face. The two bottom bays, bays 1 and 2 counted from the sill, are packed solid with sunken logs, and no water gets through them. The bays above them were clear. Nobody has cleared the logs, and there is no outage planned for that before the next campaign. My sketch of the rack face is attached.
